name: Teratogenic Pierre Robin Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of micrognathia or retrognathia (small or recessed lower jaw)
Glossoptosis causing posterior displacement of the tongue
U-shaped cleft palate or other palatal abnormalities
Respiratory difficulties due to upper airway obstruction
Feeding difficulties secondary to anatomical abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: micrognathia, glossoptosis, and cleft palate
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; genetic testing may be used to identify associated syndromes or teratogenic causes.

pathognomonic.notes: Small or recessed mandible evident at birth
Posterior displacement of the tongue causing airway obstruction
Characteristic palatal defect associated with the syndrome

searchTerms: difficulty breathing through nose or throat

common.notes: Due to impaired suck and swallow mechanisms
Secondary to feeding and respiratory issues
Middle ear infections due to Eustachian tube dysfunction
Intermittent oxygen desaturation from airway obstruction

occasional.notes: Secondary to cleft palate and hearing impairment
Malalignment of teeth due to mandibular hypoplasia
Obstructive sleep apnea due to airway abnormalities
Conductive hearing loss from middle ear pathology

rare.notes: Softening of tracheal cartilage causing airway collapse

laboratory: Genetic testing may reveal chromosomal abnormalities or teratogenic exposure markers
imaging: Airway fluoroscopy or endoscopy demonstrating glossoptosis
MRI or CT scan for airway and craniofacial anatomy assessment
genetic: No single gene mutation; may be associated with chromosomal anomalies or teratogenic exposures
Genetic counseling recommended if syndromic features present
other: Polysomnography for assessment of obstructive sleep apnea
Feeding evaluation by speech and swallow therapists

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of ocular abnormalities such as myopia and retinal detachment
Characteristic facial features distinct from isolated Pierre Robin sequence
Bilateral zygomatic hypoplasia and downward slanting palpebral fissures
Ear anomalies including microtia and hearing loss
Absence of cleft palate in some cases

redFlags: Severe airway obstruction causing cyanosis or apnea
Failure to thrive despite feeding interventions
references: Robin P. Sur une forme de fente palatine associée à une glossoptose et à une retrognathie. Bull Soc Med Hop Paris. 1923.
